look_here_first: Inspect the intact papery spathe: normally 2–3 bracts, about one vein each. The umbel usually bears 10–25 flowers; bulbils are rare.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Approved Master Plant Pool row 35; 2026-10-07 taxonomy/diagnostic review
project_inclusion.range_basis: Texas native at state level; three target-zone counties not yet verified.

morphology_keys.leaves: Basal linear leaves 10–30 cm long, 1–3(–5) mm wide.
morphology_keys.umbel: Mostly 10–25 flowers on 5–20 mm pedicels; bulbils rare.
morphology_keys.flowers: Six spreading tepals; campanulate to star-like flowers about 6–9 mm.

comparisons.key_distinctions: A. canadense usually has 3–4 more strongly multiveined spathe bracts, and may carry bulbils, but some varieties flower without bulbils. Nothoscordum lacks strong onion odor. Do not key by color or absence of bulbils alone.
